scope: Warrior 전투도끼 낙하 고정 낙하축 후면 바람결과 하강 강조선 수정본

sourcePolicy.revisionGoal: 고정 궤도와 늦은 타격 종료는 유지하면서 F07-F12의 낙하 구간에만 공격 본체 뒤로 흐르는 얇은 바람결과 하강 강조선을 추가한다.
sourcePolicy.userTemporalOverride: 이 스킬은 공통 F08-F09 타격과 F16 소실 규칙을 사용하지 않는다. 첫 접촉 F13, 최대 타격 F15, 타격 이펙트 유지 종료 F16을 유지한다.

commonPrompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: production 2D combat VFX overlay sprite sheet for AlarmQuest. Create exactly 16 chronological animation frames in a strict 4-column by 4-row, row-major sprite sheet. Every cell is one independent wide 361:160 combat viewport; final sheet 1444:640; Detailed hand-painted high-resolution 2D rendering; transparent RGBA; clean antialiased alpha; image-rendering auto; no pixel art. Keep the camera, crop, scale, contact point, perspective, blade-pressure thickness, crescent silhouette, and trajectory mathematically fixed for all sixteen cells. Motion grammar: LOCKED_AXE_SPLINE_WINDLINE_LATE_IMPACT. Define one immutable upper-right to lower-middle axe-pressure path with center samples F07=(68%,16%), F08=(65%,28%), F09=(62%,40%), F10=(59%,52%), F11=(56%,64%), F12=(53%,73%), and fixed contact P=(52%,77%). The samples progress monotonically downward and slightly left with no reversal, overshoot, sideways recoil, rotation, rescaling, or independently redrawn silhouette. Reuse one broad chipped crescent profile at the same 24-degree downward-left angle and curvature; animate only its continuous translation along the locked path, compressed motion wake, contact deformation, and attached fragments. Add a subordinate BACK AIR layer only during descent: exactly three to five thin, long, tapered, translucent wind streaks behind the crescent, all parallel to the same locked descent vector and all sharing one fixed upper-right vanishing origin. These are transparent VFX strokes inside the cell, never a scene or background panel. Their anchors and spacing remain fixed from frame to frame: F07 begins with short faint streaks; F08-F11 lengthen the same strokes monotonically behind the accelerating crescent; F12 compresses and converges those same strokes toward P without collision. Keep each streak narrower than 2% of cell width, separated by transparent corridors, low-alpha cool blue-gray or ivory, and clearly weaker than the steel-pressure edge. Do not redraw, wiggle, fork, rotate, alternate, or laterally shift the streaks. At F13 all long descent streaks terminate exactly at P and fold into one low upward gust attached to first contact. F14-F16 contain no separate long background streak layer; only short attached air tears rooted at the impact wedge may remain. User-specific late-hit choreography overrides the normal early-impact/fade contract: F01 nearly transparent. F02-F06 show restrained weight gathering only in the upper-right start zone, never a complete attack. F07-F11 descend through the exact locked samples with steadily increasing speed and weight. F12 stops a hair above P with compressed air and no collision spark, crack, or damage burst. F13 is the first physical contact at P. F14 expands the same attached contact wedge and short pressure tear. F15 is the unique maximum hit: one heavy asymmetric ochre-white impact flare, one low wide broken steel-pressure fan, five to seven short gunmetal chips, and a compact dustless compression fold, all rooted at P. F16 remains a readable impact ending tableau at 75-85% of F15 energy: keep the same contact wedge, the same flare core, and slightly separated attached chips; do not fade to transparent, recover, retract, or create a second finisher. The animation ends on the hit effect and disappears only because playback ends at 1,000ms. Use cold gunmetal, desaturated blue-gray steel pressure, ivory edge light, and restrained ochre impact accents. Keep transparent corridors and avoid an opaque full-cell wash. Treat every cell as separately clipped with no adjacent-frame residue. Render VFX only: no character, enemy, hands, complete axe, handle, weapon body, scenery, sky, ground plane, UI, text, labels, frame numbers, grid, borders, gutters, padding, or opaque background.

skills.name: 전투도끼 낙하
skills.generationPrompt: Regenerate '전투도끼 낙하' as one heavy axe-pressure crescent following the locked upper-right-to-lower-middle path without any visual shake, while adding readable but restrained wind pressure behind its fall. Preserve the approved behavior: one immutable chipped crescent silhouette, broad weight, 24-degree downward-left angle, fixed lower-middle contact point, first contact F13, maximum impact F15, and impact-held ending F16. During F07-F12 move the same crescent through the declared coordinate samples with smooth monotonic acceleration. Place exactly three to five narrow tapered air streaks on the BACK layer behind it. The streaks must be mostly vertical with the same slight leftward slant as the descent path, never horizontal and never radial. Reuse the same streak anchors every frame: start faint and short at F07, extend farther upward behind the crescent in F08-F11 to make the drop feel faster, then compress toward P at F12. The transparent gaps between streaks must remain wider than the streaks themselves, so the effect reads as wind pressure rather than a painted background. The bright core may advance along the path but cannot jump backward or sideways. F12 visibly suspends the edge just above contact. At F13 terminate all long descent streaks at P and fold their energy into one short upward gust at the first contact, so no separate background lines remain after collision. Build the attached contact wedge on F14, deliver the strongest compact impact on F15, and end F16 on that same impact. In F15-F16 lock the brightest core inside x=50%-54%, y=74%-80%; keep every chip, pressure fold, and short air tear physically rooted there. F16 is the F15 impact held and opened slightly at 75-85% energy, not a new explosion. Make the fall fast and weighty through the stable crescent, anchored descending air streaks, one short ochre-white contact flare, a broken low steel-pressure fan, and a few chunky gunmetal chips—not through camera shake, a scene background, a literal axe, a magical circle, or a huge radial blast.
